page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro system and powered by AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 Graviton processors. The machine is configured with 64 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz, featuring a single thread per core to eliminate noisy-neighbor issues from hyperthreading. System memory totals 256.0 GB, adhering to a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB allocated per core. The processor subsystem includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache.

In terms of peripheral resources, m8gb.16xlarge does not include dedicated GPU accelerators or local NVMe storage drives. Persistent storage must be provided via network-attached volumes. To support high-volume external I/O and cluster communications, the instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 133 Gbps. Cryptographic acceleration is supported via hardware AES instructions, whereas legacy x86 extensions such as AVX or AMX are absent due to the ARM architecture.

Empirical benchmarks highlight superior performance in parallel and memory-heavy execution paths. Multi-threaded evaluations show standout results, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 25794.0, a stress-ng multi-core rating of 109097.43, and top-tier metrics for Clang compilation and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The memory subsystem delivers uncached read speeds of 480.23 GB/sec and write speeds of 236.01 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core benchmarks remain in the middle tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1889.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1706.49. In artificial intelligence benchmarks, the instance handles medium and large model LLM text generation at competitive rates, while small model generation rates drop relative to peers.

Given the dedicated core count and extensive memory throughput, m8gb.16xlarge provides high resource density for workloads that scale across independent CPU cores. In-memory datastores excel on this configuration, demonstrated by Redis SET performance hitting 132 million operations per second and high static web serving throughput reaching 114.48 GB/sec. The instance is recommended for distributed caching tiers, large-scale CI/CD build environments, web serving clusters, and containerized backend microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gb.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton family, utilizing an ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, alongside 256 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server lacks bundled local storage and includes zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage while providing a baseline network bandwidth of 133 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier multi-threaded execution, evidenced by strong results in Clang software compilation, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Redis operations reaching 132 million operations per second. However, single-core CPU metrics remain moderate. The architecture provides substantial memory bandwidth and consistent execution across dedicated cores, making m8gb.16xlarge well-aligned for scalable web fleets, continuous integration and build pipelines, distributed caching layers, and general enterprise application hosting requiring wide parallelism and high network throughput.
